paper.title_en: Advancing scintillation-based dark matter detection with SiPM readout in NaI
paper.abstract_en: The ANAIS-112 experiment was designed to provide a model independent verification of the annual modulation of dark matter reported by DAMA/LIBRA using the ultra radiopure NaI(Tl) as target material at the Canfranc Underground Laboratory (LSC) in Spain. With the analysis results from six year dataset, ANAIS-112,finds no compatible modulation and strongly disfavors a dark-matter interpretation of the DAMA/LIBRA signal. A further reduction of the energy threshold is nevertheless important to make this test more robust against detector dependent effects, including uncertainties in the quenching factor mapping between nuclear-recoil and electron-equivalent energies. ANAIS+ addresses this goal by developing a low-temperature scintillation readout based on silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), replacing conventional photomultiplier tubes. This contribution presents the motivation for the ANAIS+ approach and summarizes the first prototype studies. The Octopus, SQUID and CsQUID prototypes demonstrate single-photoelectron calibration, low energy signal detection, scintillation-time characterization and temperature dependent light collection measurements in NaI and CsI crystals, supporting SiPM readout as a promising path toward lower threshold NaI based dark matter searches.
